lessons.claim: The energy recovery rate within 40 τ_int after the driving stops increases monotonically with v: −0.5±10.5 · 8±13 · 38±8 · 45±9 · 63±8 · 67±9 · 67±9 % (v = 0.1 … 32 µm/s). ★ The cause is **not** 'the faster it is the better the defects heal' -- the residual defects stay similar at 6~10. It is the **elastic/plastic ratio** of the stored energy that changes (the elastic share 31%→69%): the elastic part drains fast and the defects do not heal, so a large elastic share makes the recovery rate look high. At low speed the recovery is indistinguishable from 0 = the damage does not heal at all.

not_verified: the slow disappearance of defects outside the 40 τ_int window is unmeasured -- the accurate statement is not 'permanent' but 'it does not heal within 40 τ_int'
